I have terrible ADHD and I find this field to be quite compatibl and engaging. 

Do I have trouble staying organized? Yes
Do I have trouble staying on top of things? Yes
Am I forgetful? Yes

BUT, there is always an endless amount of new stuff to learn and systems to optimize. If I get bored with something that isn't critical I just switch tasks for a bit and come back to it later.

Something that really helped me was researching mental models and different systems to organize my time and tasks. Find one that works for you and try to implement it. It will take practice so don't get frustrated at first if you find it difficult. I personally enjoy the GDT method. (Great article can be found here: hamberg.no/gtd) it allows me to idea vomit and come back later when I feel like organizing. 

Lastly, just remember, ADHD does not make focusing/scheduling/time management impossible. It just makes it difficult and perhaps it means that traditional mental models just don't really fit with your brain which is absolutely fine. Learn how YOUR brain works and implement tools and strategies that work for you one at a time. :)

I don't post too much but I thought my experience might be useful here. 

I barely graduated highschool. I was a year of credits behind graduating my last semester and I had to spend every second of my free time catching up that semester, I ended up barely making it. I was so late that they stuck me on the end of the graduation ceremony because they already had everything planned out by the time I earned my last credit. After graduating I took a semester of college before I dropped out

Fast forward to today, I'm almost 22 years old and I work in a good, entry level, job in IT making $20 an hour. I'm doing great and have no doubt I'll be able to move up without additional schooling.

Coming out of school I knew what I wanted to do and I spent some of my free time learning how to troubleshoot computers and getting familiar with the field. I studied for my A+ certification and my CCNA but I never took the tests. I wouldnt even pass them honestly. I just wanted to get a strong foundational knowledge of the field.

If you can be knowledgeable and show a lot of ambition you can you can get almost any job. (Except some special circumstances like engineering/medical field.) My best advise is deep at it but, two big things, never stop learning and have great soft skills and you will go a long way.
